podcast.title: Transition from Jefferson Airplane (By 1974)
podcast.body: Jefferson Starship formed by 1974 after Jefferson Airplane underwent extensive "shifts in personnel." Founding member Marty Balin initially left the group due to his bandmates' "copious amounts of cocaine" and his preference for a different musical direction, away from the "psychedelic experience." "By 1974 Jefferson airplane had undergone many shifts in personnel again one would require a flow chart and it became Jefferson's starship minus however one of the band's founders Marty Ballon."

podcast.title: Departure from 1960s Counterculture Roots
podcast.body: The commercial triumph of songs like "Miracles" and albums such as *Red Octopus* represented a significant departure from the band's original 1960s counterculture ethos. Grace Slick's discomfort with performing these commercial hits underscored this tension, stating she felt "odd doing it like I was wearing a costume a monkey suit or something," and some critics longed for their earlier "Jefferson airplane back." "it's hard to believe sort of that it's that came from the same band that helped define 60s counterculture no disrespect at all to the 60s music that the band made."

podcast.title: Formation and Lineup Changes
podcast.body: Jefferson Starship was formed by Grace Slick and Paul Cantner as a revamped version of Jefferson Airplane. Marty Balin was highlighted as the "best thing about the band in the 70s," indicating his significant role during that period. "She formed with Paul Cantner, Jefferson Starship in the 70s."

podcast.title: Grace Slick's Reduced Role
podcast.body: In Jefferson Starship's 70s music, Grace Slick's role diminished significantly, primarily contributing harmonies and background vocals, such as "oh babies" on "Miracles," a stark contrast to her lead vocal prominence in Jefferson Airplane. "Grace essentially harmonized and added in some good, oh babies on that deceptively raunchy part of miracles."
